unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision drops 'For himself he knew... forced to enter supersensual chaos'. 'Every one had done it' now refers to 'thinking about it', and the next 'He' (paragraph 6) has no Adams antecedent nearby. 'The negation' lost its gloss in the first draft.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'Done it' still loosely makes sense as thinking about the unknowable, and 'a mere passenger' later restores Adams.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's 'For himself he knew that he would be forced to enter supersensual chaos...' sentence. Optionally add 'who taught that every notion included its own negation' after 'Hegel'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Essential (English thought section); the cut was not authorized.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The reader loses Adams's own commitment to the voyage, which prepares 'he found himself on the raft'. The pronoun could momentarily be read as Pearson.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Adams's personal entry into supersensual chaos is cut, blurring 'done it' and 'He recalled'

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts the plunge into Germany and the hope of renewing youth there. Germany becomes a static setting, yet 'With a deep sigh of relief, the traveller turned back' presumes a journey and frustration.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The reader can infer a trip, and Mach's going 'one step further' implies difficulty.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Change to 'He plunged into Germany, where Haeckel...', restoring the first draft clause.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Optional cuts covered only Ostwald's name; this is a dangling residue.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The navigational frame (England, Germany, France) and the comic relief of retreat lose their setup.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Germany voyage removed; 'the traveller turned back to France' dangles

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision drops two things: that Poincare alone seemed to feel the historian's need for unity, and that the second view seemed 'quite irreconcilable'. It also cuts Adams's wish to ask whether Poincare knew any history, leaving one bare sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Both contradictory quotations remain together, as the plan's risk note requires.

evidence.quote: but he seemed to be the only authority in science who felt what a historian felt so strongly--the need of unity in a universe.
he burned to ask whether M. Poincare knew any history
another view which seemed to him quite irreconcilable with the first
History and mathematics agreed. "Considering everything we have made some approach towards unity."
A mathematical paradise of endless displacement promised eternal bliss to the mathematician, but turned the historian green with horror.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore 'which seemed to him quite irreconcilable with the first'. Add one clause: 'He burned to ask whether M. Poincare knew any history.'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Essential France section; the plan's risk is satisfied but the execution is thinned.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The rise and collapse of hope is compressed. 'Turned the historian green' arrives without the historian's barbed reaction.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Poincare irony loses its hope and its retort

unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The oyster is introduced in paragraph 19, so the referents stay recoverable.
